title: First run: 38 questions with the answer written down first
changed: Ten sql questions where the answer turns on a definition: lift, new customer, regular, summer, net payout, item margin. The vendor's definitions are in the prompt. Each owner's own words are a Definitions document beside their policies, searched and cited like any other section.
Every gold query is its own file, headed by the question, so a reader can check it against the model's.

Fifteen policy questions, including two where the nearest section is the wrong one. Eight proposals that code has to check against the rules. Three questions that must be declined, one about the other restaurant, one that needs no search.

Twenty-four months of data with named menus, food costs, one price per item per channel, a promotion, loyalty rewards, seasonal items and regulars who stop coming, so these questions have answers in the data.
Retrieval threshold 0.50, a number picked from ten captured runs before this set existed.
conclusion: One wrong-but-safe query in ten. Two rules hidden by the retrieval threshold. One citation slip caught by code. The threshold moves to 0.40 next.

title: Second run: the retrieval threshold moves from 0.50 to 0.40
changed: One number changed, the similarity score a policy section needs before the model sees it, from 0.50 to 0.40. Nothing else: same questions, same gold, same model, same prompt.
conclusion: One case fewer, and a different set of failures. The rule hidden at 0.47 is now found. A question the policies do not cover now pulls in a near section, which the model dismisses correctly and my grader counts as a fail anyway. The citation slip happened a second time. Recall 86% to 93%, precision 46% to 29%. The threshold stays. The next change is the grader's rule for not-covered cases and the citation label, not the model.

title: Third run: the prompt says how to write a local-time date boundary
changed: Five lines added to the prompt, under the table that holds the restaurant's time zone: filter a date range by converting a plain timestamp literal for each boundary, and never a timestamptz literal, because that converts in the other direction. Nothing else: same questions, same gold, same model, same threshold.
Before the full run, the one failing case was run three times on its own and passed all three.
conclusion: The time zone slip is gone: ten of ten sql. Two policy cases flipped the other way for reasons that have nothing to do with the prompt line. The citation slip, which had passed the earlier case in run 1 and failed it in run 2, passed it again and failed the campaign case a third time, so that one is a coin toss until the label rule changes. The not-covered case failed as in run 2. The hidden section at 0.30 is still hidden. Next is the citation label.

title: Fourth run: the prompt says to write the whole citation label every time
changed: Two sentences added after the citing rule in the prompt: write the whole label every time, including when citing the same section again, and never shorten it to [§2] or [House Policy §2]. Nothing else changed.
Before the full run, the two cases that had slipped were run three times each on their own. All six passed the citations step.
conclusion: No short label anywhere in the run. The campaign case passed for the first time. The hidden section also came through, and not because of this change: the agent worded its second search differently and the section scored 0.51 against it, after 0.28 and 0.30 against the earlier wordings. That is the search wording deciding the answer, and one pass does not settle it. The one failure left is the not-covered case, where the answer is right and my grader's rule is wrong. Next is the grader.
